description.it: I tre sonetti di san Filippo Neri (1515-1595) conservati dal Bacci: l’anima creata da Dio e prigioniera della terra, l’amore che trasforma l’amante nell’amato, e il sonetto a Bernardino. Il testo italiano è quello dei «Documenti» di Capecelatro; per i primi due l’inglese è la versione in versi del reverendo H. I. D. Ryder, prevosto dell’Oratorio di Birmingham. Del terzo non esiste traduzione inglese libera.
description.en-US: The three sonnets of St. Philip Neri (1515-1595) preserved by Bacci: the soul made by God and imprisoned on earth, the love that changes the lover into the beloved, and the sonnet to Bernardino. The Italian is Capecelatro’s text from the Documents of his Life; for the first two the English is the verse translation by the Rev. H. I. D. Ryder, Provost of the Birmingham Oratory, as printed by Antrobus. The third has no freely available English translation.
description.pt-BR: Os três sonetos de são Filipe Néri (1515-1595) conservados por Bacci: a alma criada por Deus e prisioneira da terra, o amor que transforma o amante no amado, e o soneto a Bernardino.

it.editor: Alfonso Capecelatro (La vita di S. Filippo Neri, Milano)

en-US.translator: H. I. D. Ryder (in Bacci, Life of St Philip Neri, ed. F. I. Antrobus)

sources.edition: Alfonso Capecelatro, La vita di S. Filippo Neri, Milano 1889, vol. I, Documenti, N. III (Sonetti). Internet Archive scan, OCR text; cross-read against the Antrobus 1902 Italian for sonnets I and II.
sources.description: The three sonnets, OCR corrected by hand and by comparison with Antrobus. Two further sonnets and a fragment found after Bacci are not in a free text and are left out.
sources.tierEvidence: Capecelatro died in 1912; the 1889 printing is public domain everywhere.

sources.edition: The Life of Saint Philip Neri by Bacci, ed. F. I. Antrobus, London 1902, vol. II pp. 410-412, sonnets translated by H. I. D. Ryder. Internet Archive scan, OCR text corrected by hand.
sources.tierEvidence: Ryder died in 1907 and Antrobus in 1903; the 1902 volume is public domain everywhere.

title.en-US: Sonnet I. The soul derives from God her being high

title.en-US: Sonnet II. I love, and loving must love ceaselessly
